title: Finitely presented approximation and invariance of exceptional torsion quotients
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative ring, $h\in B$, and $N$ a finitely generated $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Suppose $N_h$ is finitely presented over $B_h$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module, def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. There exist an integer $n\geq0$, a surjection $v:B^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow N$, and a finitely generated submodule $K\subseteq\ker v$ such that $K_h=\ker(v_h)$. In particular $M=B^{\oplus n}/K$ is finitely presented, and the induced surjection $u:M\twoheadrightarrow N$ has $u_h$ an isomorphism. Moreover, for every commutative $B$-algebra $D$ and elements $a,c\in D$ with $a=\bar h c$, where $\bar h$ is the image of $h$, the map induced by $u\otimes_BD$ is an isomorphism
$$ (M\otimes_BD)/\Gamma_{(a)}(M\otimes_BD)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ (N\otimes_BD)/\Gamma_{(a)}(N\otimes_BD). $$
Here tensor products are scalar extensions [def-weil-module-base-change], and $\Gamma_{(a)}(Q)=\{x\in Q\mid a^n x=0\text{ for some }n\geq0\}$ [def-nagata-power-torsion].

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, first proof paragraph: finite-presentation replacement and comparison of the two power-torsion quotients.

proof.text: Choose generators $z_1,\ldots,z_n$ of $N$ and define $v:F=B^{\oplus n}\to N$ by $v(b_1,\ldots,b_n)=\sum_i b_i z_i$. This is surjective by the definition of finite generation. Its localization $v_h:F_h\to N_h$ is surjective: a fraction $z/h^e$ lifts to $x/h^e$ after choosing $v(x)=z$. Coordinatewise localization identifies $F_h$ with $B_h^{\oplus n}$: the inverse sends a tuple of fractions to the vector with a common denominator. In particular $F_h$ is finitely generated over $B_h$.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, first proof paragraph; explicit finite-relation and torsion calculations.

proof.text: Put $J=\ker v$. Apply exactness of localization to $J\hookrightarrow F\xrightarrow{v}N$: its localized first image is $\ker(v_h)$. The map $J_h\to F_h$ is injective as well, since a numerator in $J$ killed in $F_h$ is killed by a power of $h$ already in $J$. Thus $J_h=\ker(v_h)$ as submodules of $F_h$. Apply the finite-kernel lemma over $B_h$ to the surjection $v_h$ from the finite module $F_h$ onto the finitely presented module $N_h$. It gives finitely many generators $q_1,\ldots,q_m$ of $J_h$.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, first proof paragraph; explicit finite-relation and torsion calculations.

proof.text: Write each $q_i$ as $j_i/h^{e_i}$ with $j_i\in J$ and let $K=\sum_i B j_i\subseteq J$. Then $K$ is finitely generated. Each $q_i=h^{-e_i}(j_i/1)$ lies in the image of $K_h$; conversely that image lies in $J_h$. Hence $K_h=J_h=\ker(v_h)$. Empty generating lists are allowed. This is the explicit finite-submodule choice suppressed in the first paragraph of Tag 0810.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, first proof paragraph; explicit finite-relation and torsion calculations.

proof.text: Set $M=F/K$. The map $B^{\oplus m}\to F$ sending the $i$th basis vector to $j_i$ has image $K$, so $B^{\oplus m}\to B^{\oplus n}\to M\to0$ is a finite presentation. Since $K\subseteq J$, define $u(x+K)=v(x)$; it is well defined and surjective. Localization exactness applied to $K\to F\to M\to0$ says that $\ker(F_h\to M_h)$ is the image of $K_h$, equal to $\ker v_h$. If a class in $M_h$ maps to zero in $N_h$, represent it by $x/h^e$ from $F_h$ (lift its numerator in $M$ to $F$); then $x/h^e\in\ker v_h$, so its class in $M_h$ is zero. Surjectivity follows by lifting numerators through $u$. Thus $u_h$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, first proof paragraph; explicit finite-relation and torsion calculations.

proof.text: Write $T=\ker u$. Since $u_h$ is injective, each $t\in T$ satisfies $t/1=0$ in $M_h$, hence $h^e t=0$ for some $e$. Fix any $B$-algebra $D$ and $a=\bar h c$ as in the statement. Tensor right exactness applied to $T\to M\xrightarrow{u}N\to0$ gives a surjection $f=u\otimes_BD$ with kernel equal to the image of $T\otimes_BD$. An element of this image is a finite sum $\sum_i t_i\otimes d_i$; choose $e_i$ with $h^{e_i}t_i=0$ and put $E=\max_i e_i$ (or $0$ for an empty sum). Then $\bar h^E\sum_i t_i\otimes d_i=\sum_i (h^Et_i)\otimes d_i=0$. Therefore $a^E=c^E\bar h^E$ kills it. Thus $\ker f\subseteq\Gamma_{(a)}(M\otimes_BD)$. No flatness of $D$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, first proof paragraph; explicit finite-relation and torsion calculations.

proof.text: For any $D$-module $Q$, the set $\Gamma_{(a)}(Q)$ is a submodule: if $a^r x=0$ and $a^s y=0$, then $a^{r+s}(x+y)=0$, and $a^r(dx)=d(a^rx)=0$. Since $f$ is $D$-linear it sends power torsion to power torsion, and so induces the displayed quotient map. That map is surjective because $f$ is. If $f(x)$ is power torsion, choose $r$ with $a^r f(x)=0$. Then $a^r x\in\ker f$; by the previous step choose $s$ with $a^s(a^r x)=0$. Hence $x$ is power torsion, proving injectivity and the asserted isomorphism.
